oracle: hidden; 22 checks per task (18 permission-matrix + data-correctness, 4 migration data-preservation), written after agents launched, cookie-aware multi-session HTTP, name-agnostic; graded both arms identically
fairness_note: The direct arm's prompt named the exact failure modes to avoid (password hashing, sessions-survive-restart, ownership-403, migration-must-preserve-data). That is the security checklist Miura bakes in for free; handing it to the direct arm makes this a capability comparison, and BIASES TOWARD CORRECTNESS PARITY. See writeup.

no_checklist_rerun.what_changed: The direct arm was relaunched with ONE sentence removed — the footgun checklist (hash passwords, persist sessions, ownership 403, don't drop-and-recreate). Task, contract, oracle, and 'test however you like' all byte-identical. Isolates 'correct when you forget to ask'.

tokens.note: slightly MORE than the checklist run (290391) — agents rediscovered the footguns via their own testing

human_review_loc.note: Miura's 562 lines INCLUDE the acceptance tests; the direct arm's 2568 lines (app v1 + migrate scripts) include NO tests. Miura migration adds 0 reviewable lines (miurac migrate). Generated Miura code (3532 lines) is not reviewed.

totals.correctness_finding: Correctness parity across all three conditions (CRUD, auth+migration with checklist, auth+migration without). The predicted correctness gap did NOT appear. Robust value is cost (~1.5x tokens, ~2.8x tool calls), a 4.6x smaller test-carrying review surface, and structural (compiler-enforced, artifact-carried) vs contingent (this-episode-tested) correctness.
